segments.contextBefore: The following code shows an example that configures a background task so that the app may save data to its server, which could take longer than five seconds.
segments.documentTitle: Extending your app’s background execution time

segments.normalizedSource: ```swift func sendDataToServer(data: NSData) { // Perform the task on a background queue. DispatchQueue.global().async { // Request the task assertion and save the ID. self.backgroundTaskID = UIApplication.shared. beginBackgroundTask(withName: "Finish Network Tasks") { // End the task if time expires. UIApplication.shared.endBackgroundTask(self.backgroundTaskID!) self.backgroundTaskID = UIBackgroundTaskInvalid } // Send the data synchronously. self.sendAppDataToServer(data: data) // End the task assertion. UIApplication.shared.endBackgroundTask(self.backgroundTaskID!) self.backgroundTaskID = UIBackgroundTaskInvalid } } ```
segments.contextBefore: The [`beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:)`](uiapplication/beginbackgroundtask(withname:expirationhandler:).md) method returns an identifier that you must save and pass to the [`endBackgroundTask(_:)`](uiapplication/endbackgroundtask(_:).md) method.
segments.contextAfter: **Note**: The [`beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:)`](uiapplication/beginbackgroundtask(withname:expirationhandler:).md) method can’t be called from an app extension.
